# stochastic/testdata

Fixtures and parity goldens for `github.com/pflow-xyz/go-pflow/stochastic`.

| File | Origin |
|---|---|
| `coffeeshop.json`, `stoplight.json`, `tcp-handshake.json` | byte copies of petri-pilot `services/*.json` |
| `parity_coffeeshop_seed42.json` | `sim.Simulate(coffeeshop, nil, Options{Horizon: 8, Samples: 60, Realizations: 5, Seed: 42})` |
| `parity_sir_seed11.json` | `sim.Simulate(sir, nil, Options{Horizon: 40, Samples: 81, Realizations: 8, Seed: 11})` — the SIR net of `consistency_test.go` Case 2 (S 990, I 10, R 0; infect 0.0005 with S,I inputs and I×2 output; recover 0.1) |

The two `parity_*.json` files were generated by the **pre-move** petri-pilot
engine (`pkg/runtime/sim.Simulate` before the SSA was promoted here), with
`pkg/runtime/sim/internal/paritygolden` at petri-pilot commit

    67538d70c977fa7d6de9e0ac1f247da900b64600

`json.MarshalIndent` of the `Result`; floats are encoding/json's
shortest-round-trip form, which is exact. `parity_test.go` asserts `==` on
every float of `Times`, each `Series.Values`/`StdDev`, `Final` and
`Metrics.Throughput/Mean/P95`. A difference means the move changed the sample
path; it is never fixed by regenerating.

## `portable/` — the byte-exact SSA goldens

`portable/{chain,sir,dimer,gates,coffeeshop}.json` are the goldens for
`Options{Portable: true}`: the SSA on a fixed PRNG (SplitMix64 → xoshiro256\*\*)
and an explicit logarithm (`stochastic/portable.go`), so the same fixture
produces the same IEEE-754 doubles in Go, Rust (pflow-rs), JavaScript
(pflow-xyz) and Julia (pflow-jl). Shape, semantics and per-language notes are
the portable SSA specification, `ssa-spec.md`; each file's `_comment` names the
go-pflow commit that generated it.

Written by `cmd/ssa-goldens` — `make ssa-goldens` — and never by a test.
`portable_parity_test.go` replays every file and asserts `==` on every double
of `times`, each place's `values`/`stddev`, and `final`, plus
`final[p] == values[p][samples-1]`. A difference means the engine's sample
path changed; it is never fixed by regenerating.

| File | Options (horizon, samples, realizations, seed) | Exercises |
|---|---|---|
| `chain.json` | 10, 11, 3, 42 | two-draw loop, selection scan, grid recording, final hold |
| `sir.json` | 40, 81, 8, 11 | two kinetic inputs, weight-2 output, non-unit rates (same net as `parity_sir_seed11.json`; different stream and log, so different values — expected) |
| `dimer.json` | 5, 21, 4, 7 | `combinations()` with `w = 2`, reverse reaction, `m < w` |
| `gates.json` | 20, 41, 4, 5 | read arc, inhibitor, non-kinetic input, capacity bound, self-loop on a full place — the §3.1/§3.3 branches the spec's four fixtures never reach |
| `coffeeshop.json` | 8, 60, 5, 42 | `coffeeshop.json` stripped to the §4.1 keys; capacities, no-input transitions, `C(1000, 20)`, twelve transitions, `8/59` inexact grid |

### Provenance

The files in `portable/` were generated by `cmd/ssa-goldens` at commit

    9e67d06bf66c60ca641c8e515d15545deafcb060

(branch `discrete-stochastic`), and every `_comment` names that commit.
The generator is deterministic; if it is ever re-run, no double may change —
only the comment text — and this table, the `_comment`s and the three
consumer READMEs (pflow-rs, pflow-xyz, pflow-jl) must be refreshed together.

| File | sha256 |
|---|---|
| `chain.json` | `892de18e6c8d7899ed8a7081b0da3b1de5c4eda143f16c627ab21919cea61832` |
| `coffeeshop.json` | `2e0402f8d6e0ec32956538e480f76d6e3ec28861cb03211eb97be6a68f9f0c53` |
| `dimer.json` | `5b260cc9b3027c660d87d5a041839941f4deb1107a22728782549bc700e23341` |
| `gates.json` | `9a2a35ef18b5218a1afcda49f1755e47feb9942bf07254533971e1d490df7009` |
| `sir.json` | `192035da7d6b848479a8f2586f1330caed19c8bf26ece2f4743017aef240e683` |

The other repos carry **byte-identical copies** (`pflow-rs
crates/pflow-solver/tests/fixtures/ssa/`, `pflow-xyz parity/ssa/`, `pflow-jl
test/testdata/ssa/`), each with a README naming the go-pflow commit and the
sha256 of every file. Refresh them with `cp` after any regeneration here, and
verify with `sha256sum` on both sides against the table above.
